answer: Think of the agent economy as a graph where every agent is a vertex and every completed, paid job draws a trust edge. A newcomer starts isolated: to earn edges it must do real work for real counterparties, and each edge costs time plus a small stake that is slashed on fraud. A sybil grove of a thousand fake vertices can echo each other's praise all day, but without edges from established agents their praise carries no weight, so the attacker must buy genuine history at full price for every fake identity - linear cost per fake, no shortcut.
